## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do

`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
    bookmark the work-repo is on.
  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
    the wrong remote ref.
- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
    the squash.
  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.

A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.

**Title**

```
fix: symlink names a project as Claude Code does
```

**Body**

```
Claude Code keeps a project's session data in a directory under
~/.claude/projects named from the project's path, with every character
that is not an ASCII letter or digit replaced by a dash. The symlink
command derived that name by replacing only "/" and ".", so for a path
holding anything else, an underscore the case that was met, it made a
link Claude Code never reads.

* The name was derived by a narrower rule than Claude Code's.
  - Every character that is not an ASCII letter or digit becomes a
    dash, one per UTF-16 code unit, which is how Claude Code's own
    replace counts them.
  - A name over 200 characters, which Claude Code cuts and suffixes
    with a hash, is still left whole.
* The README did not say how the name is derived, and called the link's
  target ".claude" whatever the agent-repo directory is named.
  - The symlink section states the rule and names the target as the
    workspace's agent-repo directory.
```

content.content:
fix: clone names the agent-repo from repos.agent

Cloning a workspace whose .vc-config.md has no [remote] agent-repo
guesses the agent-repo's remote name as the work repo's name plus
".agent-session". A workspace created before the key keeps its
agent-repo under the name its agent dir was made with, iiac-perf.claude
beside repos.agent = ".claude", so the clone fails after the work side
has landed.

* The fallback is a fixed suffix the config never states.
  - The name comes from repos.agent's last path component: a dot-led one
    is appended to the work repo's name, any other is the whole name,
    and one with no last component is refused with a pointer at the
    key.
  - The URL helper always takes a name, and the fixed-suffix derivation
    is gone.
* The schema entry, the model file, the README, the comments, and
  validate-config's suggestion described a suffix fallback, some of them
  still ".claude".
  - Each describes the derivation, and the dry-run names the rule rather
    than a URL it cannot know before the work clone.

ochid: /olznztomqwkz
--files--
added	368	6f30bd23-397d-4777-98ad-2e0c77b46df0.jsonl

The rejection is not the io_uring mess: this clone is one whole cycle behind its remotes, in both repos. I changed nothing while finding this out; everything below came from read-only GitHub API calls and local reads.

## What is on the remotes

A cycle titled `fix: clone names the agent-repo from repos.agent` landed on 2026-10-01 from somewhere other than this clone, and this clone never fetched it.

| Repo | This clone's `main` | Remote `main` |
|---|---|---|
| work-repo `vc-x1` | `41b16fee` "feat: default to .agent-session" | `b83eab14`, one commit ahead |
| agent-repo `vc-x1.agent-session` | `ee4f2c51` "feat: default to .agent-session" | `b12aaf61`, one commit ahead |

The remote agent-repo commit adds a single session file, `6f30bd23-….jsonl`, and its `ochid:` points at the work commit, so the pair is a normal `vc-x1 push`. It is not in the io_uring agent-repo, whose origin correctly points at its own repo. That workspace did not cause this.

## What it means for today's cycle

The commit I just pushed sits on the stale `main`, so it cannot land as it is:

- **Version collision:** the remote cycle already took 0.84.17, the version today's commit carries. Ours has to become 0.84.18.
- **`TODO.md` conflict:** both commits rewrite `## Closed`, and the remote one changed 41 lines of the file.
- **`README.md` and `Cargo.lock`:** both touched; README may merge cleanly, since the remote changed only two lines.
- **`src/symlink.rs`:** not touched by the remote commit, so the fix itself is unaffected.

Your two `validate-desc` runs are consistent with this: they only look at local history, which is internally fine.

## What I recommend

1. Fetch both repos (`jj git fetch` in each). This only adds the remote commits; nothing local is rewritten.
2. Rebase the work-repo commit onto the fetched `main`, resolve `TODO.md` and the version, re-validate, and show you the result for review.
3. Force-push the bookmark, which is a remote rewrite and needs your approval at that point.
4. Rebase the agent-repo commit onto its fetched `main` and squash-push it. The session files are different files, so this should not conflict.

The agent-repo commit keeps its change id through the rebase, so the `ochid:` trailers stay valid.

## One thing only you can answer

Where did the 2026-10-01 cycle come from? There are several other clones on this machine (`vc-x1-clone`, `vc-x1-main`, and others). If one of them is the live working copy and this directory is the stale one, you may prefer to continue there rather than repair this one.

Do you want me to go ahead with step 1, the two fetches?

The rebase ran and left one conflicted file, `TODO.md`; I have not resolved anything.

## Result

- **Graph:** today's commit (`wlnlztronxqq`, now `cd60e9a1`) sits on top of the fetched `main`, with the empty working copy above it. The bookmark moved with it locally and is now ahead of its remote copy, which is unchanged.
- **Merged cleanly:** `src/symlink.rs`, `README.md`, `notes/todo-backlog.md`, `Cargo.lock`, and the rest of `TODO.md` outside `## Closed`.
- **Conflicted:** `TODO.md` only, six hunks, all inside `## Closed` (lines 1183 to 1332). Both commits deleted the old "feat: default to .agent-session" block and wrote their own cycle's block in its place.

## One clean merge that is still wrong

`Cargo.toml` did not conflict, because both commits made the identical edit, 0.84.16 to 0.84.17. So the rebased commit carries the same version as `main`. It needs to be 0.84.18, with `Cargo.lock` following.

## Proposed next operation

Resolve `## Closed` by keeping today's block and dropping the 2026-10-01 block. That is what an opening does anyway: it deletes whatever `## Closed` holds, and the earlier cycle's record stays in its own landed commit. Mechanically: `jj new` on the conflicted commit is already the state we are in, so I edit `TODO.md` in the working copy, show you the resolved section, and squash it into the commit only after you have seen it.

The version bump would be a separate operation after that. Shall I do the `TODO.md` resolution?

+### fix: symlink names a project as Claude Code does
 
 #### Problem
 
-`vc-x1 clone` of a workspace whose `.vc-config.md` has no `[remote] agent-repo` guesses the
-agent-repo's remote name as the work repo's name plus `.agent-session`. A workspace created before
-the key keeps its agent-repo under another name, `iiac-perf.claude` beside
-`repos.agent = ".claude"`, so the guess names a repo that does not exist and the clone fails after
-the work side landed.
+Claude Code names a project's directory under `~/.claude/projects` by replacing every character of
+the working directory's path that is not an ASCII letter or digit with `-`. The symlink code
+replaced only `/` and `.`, so for a path holding any other character, an underscore the one that
+was met, it made a link Claude Code never reads.
 
 #### Solution
 
-With no `[remote] agent-repo`, clone derives the name from the agent dir the same config declares
-in `repos.agent`, by its last path component: a dot-led component is appended to the work repo's
-name (`.claude` gives `iiac-perf.claude`), any other is the whole name (`../iiac-perf-agent` gives
-`iiac-perf-agent`), and a dir with no last component is refused with a pointer at the key. The
-fixed `.agent-session` fallback is gone, so the URL helper always takes a name. The schema entry,
-the model file, the README's table note, the comments, and `validate-config`'s suggestion, which
-still said `.claude`, describe the derivation, and the dry-run names the rule rather than a URL it
-cannot know before the work clone.
+`encode_path` applies Claude Code's rule, one dash per UTF-16 code unit as its regex counts them,
+and the README's `symlink` section states the rule.
 
 #### Acceptance check
 
-Passed:
-
-- `url.rs` tests show a dot-led dir appended to the work name, a plain dir used whole, with and
-  without `.git`, and an unnameable dir refused.
-- `clone_without_remote_agent_repo_names_it_from_the_agent_dir` clones a fixture whose config has
-  `repos.agent = ".claude"` and no `[remote] agent-repo`, beside a `remote-work.claude.git` and no
-  `.agent-session` one, and succeeds.
-- `vc-x1 clone https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf`, run into a scratch dir, cloned
-  `iiac-perf.claude` into `iiac-perf/.claude`.
-- `vc-x1 validate` passes.
+- `encode_path("/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/io_uring-2-zcr-v4-x1")` returns
+  `-home-wink-data-prgs-rust-io-uring-2-zcr-v4-x1`, the name of the link Claude Code reads for that
+  project, checked by `encode_path_with_underscore`. Passed.
+- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed.
 
 #### Deliberation
 
-- The agent dir, not a fixed suffix: wink's proposal, joining `repos.agent` with the work URL.
-  - It resolves both known workspaces: iiac-perf's `.claude` and vc-x1's `.agent-session`, which
-    init writes as the dir and the recorded name alike, so a new workspace's dir and its derived
-    name agree by construction.
-  - The alternative, trying `.claude` after `.agent-session`, probes the network and hides a
-    config that is silent about its remote.
-- The last component, split on its lead: `repos.agent` is a path, `"../x"` or absolute as well as
-  `.claude`, so "join" is defined only for a dot-led name. A dot-led component is a suffix and any
-  other is a name, one rule for every layout, as agreed with wink.
-- Single-step: one behavior change and its documentation.
-- Waiver: wink granted permission for what the cycle needs, the bookmark's publish and the
-  cycle's one push included, and reviews the work and the description before Land, in place of
-  the per-rung reviews. Land is outside the waiver.
-- Bookmark name: `fix-clone-derives-the-agent-repo-name-from-reposagent`, the slug of a first
-  title published with the bookmark and then shortened to fit the title cap.
-- The suggestion's text is in scope: `validate-config`'s nag for a missing key described the
-  fallback, wrongly since the last cycle, so it changes with the fallback it describes.
+- The general rule, not an underscore case: wink's entry asked for `_` to become `-`, and the
+  installed Claude Code (2.1.295) carries `replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g,"-")`, so the underscore is one
+  instance.
+  - Adding `_` as a third character leaves a space, `+`, `@`, and every non-ASCII letter as the next
+    bug.
+- Code units, not characters: the regex runs over UTF-16, so a character outside the Basic
+  Multilingual Plane is two dashes, and `encode_path` counts the same way.
+- The long-path hash is left out: Claude Code cuts a name over 200 characters to 200 and appends a
+  hash of the path.
+  - Reproducing it means copying Claude Code's hash function exactly, and no path here is near 200.
+  - It is the backlog entry [symlink names a path over 200 characters as Claude Code
+    does](notes/todo-backlog.md#symlink-names-a-path-over-200-characters-as-claude-code-does).

The note is written at the top of `TODO.md > ## Continuation notes`, as an uncommitted edit in the work-repo working copy. It covers what happened, where each repo stands, the remaining operations in order, and the two change ids that tie the pair together. The two older open questions are kept below it.

On resume versus reacquaint, I lean the same way you do: reacquaint.

## Why reacquaint

- **My picture of the agent-repo will be stale.** A resumed session carries this conversation's view of that repo from before your sync. A fresh one reads the real state and has nothing to unlearn.
- **This context is long and mostly detour.** Most of it is the diagnosis, which is now settled and summarised in the note. The remaining work is five small, well-defined operations.
- **It is the designed path.** Continuation notes exist for exactly this hand-off, and using them is also the test of whether the note is good enough.
- **It exercises acquaint against a mid-repair state.** If acquaint handles this cleanly, that is useful evidence for the "check the remotes at acquaint" idea.

## What resume would buy

Only convenience: no re-read, and the approved description and review history are still in view. Neither is needed, since the description is already in the commit and the remaining steps do not change it.

## The risk in reacquainting, and how the note covers it

The next session must not treat the rebased commit as fresh work to re-review or re-describe, and must not assume the force-push is approved. The note says both: the work and description are done and approved, the commit is amended by squash and never re-described, and the force-push needs its own approval.

One suggestion: read the note yourself before exiting. It is the only thing the next session gets, so if anything in it reads wrong or thin to you, it is cheaper to fix now than to explain later.

content.content:
vc-x1 0.84.17

Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.

Repo set is resolved (in order):
  - `-R` / `--repo`     exact list (back-compat / arbitrary multi-repo)
  - `--scope=work|agent|work,agent` dual-repo roles via `.vc-config.toml`
  - neither             default: `work,agent` when dual, else `work`

One atomic operation: fetch, then per repo:
  - up-to-date        nothing to do
  - behind            fast-forward bookmark to remote
  - ahead             nothing to sync (local has unpushed work)
  - diverged          rebase local onto remote; fail on conflicts
  - no remote         bookmark has no @<remote> counterpart; skip

After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced
bookmark: the work repo `jj new`s a clean `@` (or rebases a
dirty one with --rebase / a prompt), the `.claude` session
repo `jj new main`s when main moved (no-op when `@-` is
already the main tip).

On failure sync stops where the failing step stopped: nothing
is auto-reverted, so the state can be inspected. The failure
report prints each repo's pre-sync op id; undo explicitly with
`jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. Nothing persists across
invocations.

Output shape:
  - all-up-to-date: one-line summary (`sync: N repos are up to date, nothing to
  sync`)
  - action needed:  per-repo fetch + state + actions
  - --quiet:        no output; exit code signals success

Usage: vc-x1 sync [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -q, --quiet
          Suppress all informational output (exit code signals result)

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to sync in the work repo. The session (bot) repo is a linear
          journal and always syncs `main`, regardless
          
          [default: main]

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --remote <REMOTE>
          Remote to sync against
          
          [default: origin]

      --rebase
          Rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced bookmark without asking.
          
          After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced bookmark.
          When the work repo's `@` carries changes it normally asks before
          rebasing, and `--rebase` answers yes up front for non-interactive use.
          Ignored for the bot repo (which always `jj new main`).

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Workspace root, or a single jj repo to sync on its own.
          
          - `-R PATH` alone: sync just the repo at PATH.
          - `-R PATH -s ROLES`: use PATH as the workspace root and
            sync the named side(s).

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repo(s) of the workspace to sync.
          
          `SCOPE=work|agent|both`:
          
          - `work`: sync only the work repo.
          - `agent`: sync only the bot repo (errors if no bot repo
            is configured).
          - `both` (or `work,agent`): sync both repos.
          
          Composes with `-R` as the workspace root. Default depends
          on workspace state: dual workspace -> `work,agent`, and a
          single-repo workspace or POR -> `work`.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

content.text:
`vc-x1 sync` is the right tool, and I read its code to check it does what this case needs. Use the scoped form from the workspace root rather than `cd`-ing in:

```
vc-x1 sync -R .agent-session
vc-x1 squash-push -R .agent-session
```

## What sync will do here

- **Fetch**, then classify the agent-repo's `main` as diverged: local has today's commit, remote has the laptop's.
- **Rebase** the local branch onto `main@origin` (a `rebase -b`, so the working copy above it comes along with whatever session data it holds).
- **Stop if the rebase conflicts**, leaving the state in place and printing the pre-sync op id with the `jj op restore` undo. I do not expect a conflict: the laptop's commit adds one file that does not exist here.
- **Not push.** Sync only brings local level with the remote; the `squash-push` afterwards is what publishes, and it also folds in the session data this conversation has written since the failed push.

The rebase keeps the change id `nqznqryqlrpp`, so the work commit's `ochid:` stays valid. You can confirm afterwards with `vc-x1 validate-desc @.. -n 3 -R .agent-session`.

## Why scoped, not `cd .agent-session; vc-x1 sync`

Run bare, sync finds the workspace root and syncs both repos, wherever you start it. For the work-repo that would be harmless today: `main` is already up to date, and the code leaves the working copy alone when it is not behind the bookmark. But `-R .agent-session` touches only the repo you mean to fix, which is the safer habit while the work-repo is mid-repair with an uncommitted note in it.

## Caveat

I read the code path; I did not run it. This divergence is exactly the case sync's diverged branch is written for, but if the output says anything other than "diverged … rebase needed" followed by a rebase line, stop and look before running the squash-push.

content.text:
Yes: `cd .agent-session; vc-x1 sync -R .` syncs only the agent-repo. In the code, `-R PATH` with no `--scope` returns exactly that one path and never looks up the workspace, so `.` there means the agent-repo and nothing else. It is equivalent to `vc-x1 sync -R .agent-session` from the root.

The agent side is still recognised from inside the directory (the path is canonicalised before the check), so it gets the agent-repo treatment: `main` only, and the working copy repositioned with the journal rule.

## On the default

The no-flag behaviour is deliberate rather than a bug: bare `vc-x1 sync` means "sync this workspace", both repos, from wherever you stand in it. But there is a real inconsistency behind your surprise:

- **`sync` and `revert`:** no flags means the workspace's default scope, both repos in a dual workspace.
- **The read-only commands (`chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`):** no flags means `.`, just the repo you are in.

So the same "no flags" means two different things depending on the command, which is easy to forget. Your existing entry "squash-push and status take a SCOPE, and push resolves its own bookmarks" and "Global -R anchors the workspace for every command" are the natural homes for settling that; I would add a line to one of them rather than open a new entry. Say if you want it noted, and it can go in with the version-bump edit next session.

As before, I read this from the code and did not run it.
